shared: no expected result is given to any system

b3WhenSomethingIsDeclared.detail: the fixture declares no assurance, so B3 on these scenarios is A3 with an empty list. Given a reference it actually relied on, B3 re-runs that consumer and answers identically for one more evaluation. Consuming a declaration is not free.

lineCounts.note: physical lines including comments, the count a team would pay for. The engine lines were removed from the Kernel's shipped surface; they are counted here to price what was removed

notMeasured: no IntentLane path: the application mechanism was not run against a real consumer
no Sarah path: the fixture is invented arithmetic, not a real operator
no Apple path: no public surface was exercised
no human utility: nothing here measures whether anyone is better served
no generative DAG: the fixture is closed and hand-checkable
no M2 or M3 cross-system comparison: this is the incremental scope only
no M4: the decision in ADR-003 was to measure before building, not to build

conditionClauses.clause: A3 and B3 reach the same observable result as C3 on every scenario
conditionClauses.evidence: all 7 scenarios agreed with the full recompute

conditionClauses.clause: the core saves nothing the application could not already do
conditionClauses.evidence: NOT MET. On 1 of 7 scenarios the core ran fewer evaluators than the application, by 2 runs in total, because a consumed facet is a narrower key than a whole value.
the saving is 2 evaluator runs on a closed 3-evaluator fixture, bought with 1542 lines of engine against 247 lines of application

recommendation.decisionRests: Two of the three pre-registered clauses are met outright. The third is not, and it is the only measured advantage the core has over a competent application. The reduction is therefore a decision not to pay for capability that nothing measured, on the strength of one small measured saving that a consumer could buy back for a fraction of the price. It is not a claim that the capability is worthless.
recommendation.falsifier: The reduction would be wrong if A3 had to grow a facet comparator, a disposition or an obligation to pass these scenarios. It did not have to. The one difference the core does buy, a consumed facet, is available to the application for a fraction of the lines, and on a graph with many unconsumed fields that advantage would grow rather than shrink, which is the case to re-measure before anyone rebuilds this.
recommendation.preRegisteredCondition: A3 and B3 reach the same observable result as C3 on every scenario, and the core saves nothing the application could not already do at a comparable price.
recommendation.text: Reduce the Kernel to UNI plus adapters and stop building M4.
whatGoes: src/impact, as a mechanism any consumer would build for itself, moved to tests/support/impact_core so the measurement can be repeated
M4, which would have added story to a scope with no measured value
whatSurvives: the five impact dimensions, because they keep a consumer from collapsing them
the obligation, because an application cache cannot tell a consumer that work is owed
the disposition, because a cache reports a value and not what happened to it
the explanation, because a cache cannot say why a consumer was kept
consumer-granted profiles, because a cache decides its own competence
the decision rule, because a cache would recompute a recorded human decision
